decisions.rationale: Mega Gengar (Shadow Tag) is the intended Mega. Lead Klefki+Gengar: Klefki sets Reflect (Prankster priority) to blunt Blaziken's Flare Blitz; Gengar Mega Evolves to trap Blaziken. Turn 2 Klefki TWaves Blaziken (Prankster first) while Gengar attacks to break Focus Sash. Back: Gyarados (Intimidate+SE Waterfall on Blaziken) and Rotom-Heat (SE Overheat on Tinkaton, resists Fire/Electric, Will-o-Wisp). Volt Switch bypasses Shadow Tag but Blaziken lacks a pivot move and stays trapped.
decisions.notebook: Volt Switch bypasses Shadow Tag (switches out even if trapped) — Rotom-W can escape but Blaziken/Tinkaton/Archaludon/Arcanine/Garchomp cannot (no pivot moves). Gengar-Mega Speed 200 (Timid 252); Scarf Rotom-W 174-226 (investment unknown, likely outspeeds). Gengar-Mega has no SE move vs Blaziken or Tinkaton (Shadow Ball neutral on both). Gyarados Waterfall 2x SE on Blaziken but 4x weak to Rotom-W Volt Switch — never lead Gyarados into Rotom-W. Rotom-Heat Overheat 2x SE on Tinkaton, resists Fire/Electric, weak to Hydro Pump. Opponent likely brings Blaziken+Rotom-W+Tinkaton+Archaludon for G3. Plan: trap+TWave Blaziken with Gengar-Mega+Klefki, clean up with Gyarados+Rotom-Heat. If Gengar falls, Shadow Tag ends — ensure Blaziken is paralyzed/damaged before Gengar faints.

decisions.rationale: Lead Tinkaton + Archaludon to immune Prankster T-Wave and safely handle Gengar-Mega/Klefki. Archaludon's special moves bypass King's Shield contact penalty vs Aegislash, and Thunderbolt 4x hits Gyarados. Backline Garchomp + Arcanine provides Intimidate support and a safe win condition without risking Speed Boost copy by Ditto.
decisions.notebook:
Opponent game 2 bring: Gengar-Mega, Klefki, Gyarados, Rotom-Heat. Bench: Aegislash, Ditto.
Game 3 plan: Lead Tinkaton + Archaludon. Both immune to Klefki's Prankster T-Wave. Archaludon uses special moves to avoid King's Shield Attack drop vs Aegislash, and Thunderbolt 4x hits Gyarados. Keep Blaziken on bench to avoid Ditto copying Speed Boost. Use Garchomp as primary win condition with Expert Belt. Arcanine provides Intimidate support.

decisions.rationale: Archaludon Dark Pulse can OHKO Gengar (60-140%) and Gengar lacks Protect. Prankster TWave (priority,90%) goes first to paralyze Archaludon; Mega Gengar at 200 Spe outspeeds both foes and Focus Blasts (2x SE, 72-139%) for likely KO. 63% both hit = Archaludon neutralized. If Archaludon Protects, Gengar only takes Knock Off (26-70%, survives). Shadow Tag traps both regardless. Tinkaton can be dealt with next turn while trapped.
decisions.notebook: Mold Breaker does NOT negate Prankster (not in nullified list) — Klefki TWave keeps priority vs Tinkaton. Archaludon Dark Pulse can OHKO Gengar (60-140% w/ Life Orb). Gengar Focus Blast does 72-139% to Archaludon (possible OHKO). Gengar has no Protect — must neutralize threats proactively. If Gengar gets paralyzed by Tinkaton TWave, Mega speed 200 drops to 50 (outspeeded by everything). Prioritize keeping Gengar alive to maintain Shadow Tag. Opponent backline: Garchomp (EQ+RockSlide), Arcanine (FlareBlitz+Intimidate), Rotom-W (Scarf+VoltSwitch escapes Shadow Tag), Blaziken (Sash+SpeedBoost). Win con: trap with Shadow Tag, paralyze speed threats, clean up with Gyarados+Rotom-Heat.

decisions.rationale: Gyarados is the clear send: Intimidate immediately weakens Tinkaton's Knock Off/Play Rough, Flying typing grants EQ immunity vs Garchomp, Water resists Flare Blitz and Flying resists Close Combat from Blaziken. Speed 146 outspeeds Careful Tinkaton (114-146, unlikely max). Main risk is Rock Slide from Garchomp, but Gyarados can Protect next turn while Klefki sets screens or TWaves. Rotom-Heat lacks Intimidate and is slower, offering less immediate board impact.

Klefki at 100% with Reflect/Light Screen/TWave/Dazzling Gleam all available. Opponent remaining: Tinkaton (100%, Mold Breaker, Sitrus, Careful), Garchomp (Jolly, ExpertBelt, RoughSkin), Arcanine (Adamant, Leftovers, Intimidate), Rotom-W (Timid, ChoiceScarf, Levitate — can Volt Switch out), Blaziken (Jolly, FocusSash, SpeedBoost). Win con: paralyze speed threats with Klefki Prankster TWave, set screens, sweep with Gyarados (DDance) + Rotom-Heat. Watch for Garchomp Rock Slide on Gyarados (2x). Gyarados immune to EQ. Rotom-Heat immune to EQ via Levitate. Key speed tiers: Gyarados 146, Rotom-Heat 138, Klefki 95. Tinkaton 114-146 (Careful, likely not max speed). Blaziken Speed Boost after turn 1 outspeeds everything — must paralyze or KO before it boosts.

decisions.rationale: Double super-effective damage on Gengar aims to KO it before it can act. Archaludon's Life Orb Dark Pulse should KO Gengar, and Tinkaton's Knock Off provides backup. Both my Pokémon are immune to Prankster T-Wave, and Archaludon's Sturdy ensures it survives any hit from full HP.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Gengar + Klefki. Gengar likely Mega Evolves turn 1. Both my leads are Steel-type, immune to Prankster T-Wave. Archaludon's Sturdy prevents KO from full HP. Garchomp and Arcanine on bench for later.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp guarantees outspeeding Klefki (169 vs 95-127) and OHKOs with Earthquake before Prankster screens go up. Arcanine's 117 Speed loses to max-Speed Klefki, allowing Reflect to negate Flare Blitz. Garchomp also pressures Rotom-Heat and Aegislash on future turns.

Priority: KO Klefki before screens, preserve Garchomp for Gyarados/Rotom, use Arcanine Intimidate vs physical threats.

decisions.rationale: Reflect is the single best action: it prevents Garchomp EQ from KOing Klefki (70-100%→35-50%) and softens Rock Slide on Gyarados (39-55%→19-27%). Gyarados Dragon Dances behind the screen, reaching219 Spe which outspeeds Garchomp's 134-169 max. Next turn Klefki can Prankster TWave Garchomp or Tinkaton while Gyarados sweeps. Risk: Tinkaton TWave on Gyarados, but Reflect keeps us alive and Rotom-Heat is backup.

decisions.rationale: Rock Slide is 2x on Gyarados with Expert Belt boost, pressuring the Life Orb attacker immediately. Klefki's Prankster status goes first but we still get both moves off, spreading damage and crippling Gyarados's speed tier.

Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Protect blocks Overheat/Thunderbolt/Will-O-Wisp and forces Rotom-Heat to commit. If it Protects, we stall safely; if it attacks, we live and reposition next turn.

decisions.rationale: Overheat is SE (2x) into Tinkaton at 70% HP, dealing 71.4-125%—guaranteed KO on hit. Rotom outspeeds paralyzed Tinkaton (138 vs 57-73). Tinkaton Protect has reduced success after 3 uses; Overheat 90% acc is the only risk. This is the series-winning play.

reflections.summary: Won through clean execution with zero decision errors. Klefki's screens and Thunder Wave spread bought enough time for Gyarados to remove Garchomp with Waterfall, and Rotom-Heat cleaned up the paralyzed Tinkaton with Overheat. The opponent's Protect-heavy stall cracked when double-Protect chains failed on consecutive turns (Tinkaton turn 12), opening the KO window.
reflections.adjustment: Gengar-Mega contributed nothing visible across 12 turns and the win relied on Rotom-Heat at 36% as the sole survivor. If a similar opponent appears, consider whether Gengar-Mega's slot is better used by a bulkier cleaner or a second Intimidate user; the four-brought composition won but had thin margins and no real Mega value.
reflections.notebook: Opponent roster fully revealed: Garchomp (Jolly/ExpertBelt/RoughSkin), Tinkaton (Careful/Sitrus/MoldBreaker), Arcanine (Adamant/Leftovers/Intimidate), Archaludon (Modest/LifeOrb/Sturdy), Rotom-Wash (Timid/ChoiceScarf/Levitate, not brought G3), Blaziken (Jolly/FocusSash/SpeedBoost, not brought G3). Opponent tendencies: Protect-heavy stall with double-Protect chains, Rock Slide flinch fishing from Garchomp, Thunder Wave + Will-O-Wisp spread for speed/attack control, Mold Breaker Tinkaton ignores abilities (relevant vs Levitate/Intimidate). Opponent benched speed control (Scarf Rotom-W) and setup sweeper (Sash Blaziken) in the decisive game, opting for bulky paralysis stall. Series result: won 2-1. Future plan: vs this opponent, prioritize Taunt/Safeguard over raw screens to disrupt TWave spread; Mold Breaker Tinkaton is the key threat to ability-dependent mons (Rotom, Gyarados Intimidate); expect Protect chains and play for double-Protect reads.

reflections.summary: Lost because the team preview brought Garchomp into a Klefki + Gyarados core that completely neutralized it—Klefki outspeeds and KO's with Dazzling Gleam, and Gyarados is immune to Earthquake and outspeeds with Waterfall. This left my primary attacker useless, and the remaining team (Tinkaton, Archaludon) lacked sufficient answers to the opponent's Gyarados and Rotom-Heat win conditions.
reflections.adjustment: Against Klefki + Gyarados cores, do not bring Garchomp (liability into both). Lead Archaludon to threaten Gyarados with Thunderbolt and resist Klefki's Fairy moves, and use Arcanine to pressure Klefki with Flare Blitz.
